note: RE-RUN. Grok's domains.retrieval grew from 5 to 8 mechanisms: confirmed-corruption-quarantine-and-recreate and debounced-hash-deduped-index-maintenance (xai-grok-session-search) and two-tier-index-lock-with-stale-takeover (xai-codebase-graph). The first two join the session-corpus search/index row, the third joins the codebase index row; none is an agent-written durable-memory mechanism, so the session-search versus durable-memory split is preserved. Caveats that referred to an uninventoried grok column are removed. The previous run's attachment-modality-gating row is consolidated into the image normalization/request-projection row, which drops the row count from 29 to 28; no other row changed membership. Coverage is 68 placed mechanisms, up from 65 because grok's retrieval array grew from 5 to 8; every source's array is placed in full (ih 3, dsh 14, codex 8, opencode 8, opencode-fork 8, grok 8, cc-custom 19).

They are kept in this row rather than split into an index-maintenance row so that the row states the whole session index capability; IH lacks grok's corruption classification, quarantining and settling signal (bootstrapping:true), which is real but additive and does not change the disposition.

unmergedDoubts.whyNotMerged: Both push a session out of the harness, but one is a self-contained local ZIP of the durable log streamed over a host route and the other is a debounced upload to a hosted collaboration service with account/org auth; merging would hide that dsh needs no service and opencode needs one.

Name collision on 'reference' only: dsh injects a budgeted, untrusted snapshot of ANOTHER SESSION into the current step, while opencode materializes configured extra directories/git repositories into a cache the agent may read. Different objects, different trust story.

Placement judgement on grok's new lock: two-tier-index-lock-with-stale-takeover is a generic index-work serializer, so it could have been read as an index-maintenance member of the session-corpus row. It is placed with the codebase-graph row instead because its only module is xai-codebase-graph, its lock file sits beside the codebase-graph cache, and its shipped consumer is the codebase index background refresh; the session row's new members are all xai-grok-session-search and its SQLite session_docs table. No row mixes a session-corpus index with a repository symbol index.

cc-custom answers 'which past session is relevant' with a small-model selector over a packed manifest (title/branch/summary/first-prompt/excerpt), not with a lexical index or a scan. Treating an LLM selection pass as the same capability as a BM25/FTS index would hide a genuinely different retrieval paradigm, so it stays single-source. Grok's two new session-search members are index lifecycle for the FTS index and do not narrow this gap.

codex bundles ingestion (path to portable data URL) and request-time image budgeting (detail modes, max dimension/patches) in one mechanism, so it can sit in either the ingestion row or the normalization row but not both; it is placed with ingestion and the budget half is left uncrossed. opencode's attachment-modality-gating no longer sits in this doubt as a separate row: it is now consolidated into the normalization/request-projection row, leaving only codex's inseparable bundling as the unresolved part.

dsh's live-preferred corpus read/trace engine could arguable sit with the listing/lineage surface instead of the search row: it folds titles and walks ancestry. It is placed with search because it is the read model the FTS index extends in the same service, which is how IH bundles read+search+lineage in one mechanism; a reader wanting the split should note this is a judgement call.

A standalone 'model-generated session titles' row was considered and rejected: IH's only title mechanism is bundled inside its listing/retrieval-surface mechanism, so a titles-only row would have had no ih member and could not honestly be marked 已存在 even though IH does generate titles.

cc-custom's identifier parser covers the resume surface (sessionId, ingress URL, .jsonl path) but also classifies session-memory and transcript paths under the config directory for the permission layer. Folding it into the session-list row would bury a safety-facing classification inside a retrieval row.

Both touch MCP resources, but cc-custom exposes list/read TOOLS for resources with an LRU cache and change-notification invalidation, whereas opencode-fork only ingests an already-named resource into prompt attachments.

The reverse scanner is the read primitive underneath codex's name lookup and search surfaces; it is kept as its own row because it is a reusable bounded-read guarantee (new_at freeze, oversized-record skip, rejected-not-fatal JSON), not a retrieval capability itself.

Cross-cutting rule-4 issue, not a merge question: IH demonstrably implements ripgrep search tools, web-search provider selection, an askUser/question-provider seam and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction discovery, but all four sit in IH's tools/context/service domains, so rule 1 forbids citing them as ih members here and rule 4 forbids 已存在 on a row with no ih member. Those rows are marked 路線差異 (IH structures the same capability elsewhere) rather than falsely claiming a gap.
